articleTitle: Microwave Tomography Based on Phase Difference from Small-Interval Antenna Slippage
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Multi-target echo positions in two dimensions can be achieved by combining time-domain signals of vector network analyzer (VNA) (using two ports and two antennas) and orderly variation of optical path contributed from singleantenna slippage. In this study, the positioning formulas are derived from the concept that is similar to Bragg's law of X-ray diffraction. To effectively obtain multi-echo two-dimensional image, an approach similar to Klimontovich equation in plasma physics is adopted. The proposed method has successfully been verified by a series of randomly arranged three-target experiments. The image reconstruction results precisely showed the positions of the targets.

articleTitle: Microwave Tomography Based on Time of Flight of Signals from Scattering
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Multi-target echo positions in two dimensions can be achieved by combining time of flight (TOF) of signals gathering from vector network analyzer (VNA) and two kinds of geometric placements of two antennas (quasi-mono-static and bi-static). In this study, the positioning formulas are derived simply on the basis of triangular geometry. To effectively obtain multi-echo image, an approach similar to Klimontovich equation in counting plasma density is adopted. The proposed method has successfully been verified by a series of randomly arranged three-target experiments. The image reconstruction results precisely showed the positions of the targets in assistance with reference target.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Screening: Impact of Antenna Array Configurations on Microwave Imaging Quality
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Microwave imaging (MWI) is a promising noninvasive technique for breast cancer screening, utilizing differences in dielectric properties between tissues to generate images. This study focuses on developing a robust imaging pipeline to optimize the design of specialized antenna arrays, enhancing measurement efficiency and reducing image reconstruction time. Simulations were conducted in the 1-5 GHz frequency range using a simplified breast model consisting of a single layer of skin surrounding a homogeneous healthy tissue, with a tumor target embedded within the background material. To test our pipeline, we used different antenna distributions for data acquisition. Additionally, we varied the dielectric properties of the background, the number of tumors, and their size and location. To streamline the simulation workflow, the models were built in HFSS, and simulations were processed on Compute Canada's supercomputer, allowing for efficient computation in a short time frame. Images were reconstructed using a delay-andsum (DAS) radar-based imaging algorithm called MERIT. Metrics such as signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and location error were then used to assess image quality. Our preliminary findings indicate that while non-equally spaced antennas show potential for detecting targets near the sensors, equally spaced configurations consistently yield superior image quality. This work lays the groundwork for strategic diagnostic hardware design, aiming to improve MWI accuracy through refined antenna array configurations.

articleTitle: 290 GHz Bow-Tie Slot Array Antenna for Communication and Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 \times 4$</tex> slot array antenna designed using a higher-order mode architecture, composed of five metallic layers. The design explores the filter coupling matrix of this framework and incorporates bowtie slots to enhance resonance frequency matching. The proposed antenna achieves a peak gain of 17.5 dBi and a -10 dB bandwidth spanning from 281 GHz to 297 GHz. The antenna is useful for terahertz communication and sensing applications.

articleTitle: Spoof Localized Surface Plasmon Polariton for Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This work proposes a novel Spoof Localized Surface Plasmon Polariton (SLSPP) based resonator for sensing applications using GaAs IPD (Integrated Passive Device) technology. The resonator is designed using stepped-width unit cells and is rotated at a multiple of 45 - and 90 -degree angles to form 8 arms arranged symmetrically. The proposed spoof localized surface plasmon resonator is excited by a spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) based transmission line. The designing is done considering the design rules of GaAs IPD technology. The proposed structure can be tuned from the microwave to the terahertz domain by varying the geometrical parameters. The sensor shows a good variation in transmission frequency of around 5.5 GHz when the dielectric value placed on the resonator varies from 5 to 10. These resonators can be easily integrated and have a wide range of applications in the terahertz sensing domain.

articleTitle: Generalized Radar-Based Detection of Respiratory Abnormalities in Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study investigates the use of various types of radar to recognize respiratory abnormalities in an indoor environment. Unlike prior approaches limited to fixed scenarios, our approach accommodates not only diverse measured angles and distances of the subject but also radar setups, exposing a Machine Learning method to a wide range of signal properties. Utilizing classical feature engineering and optimized hyperparameters, data from different radar types-Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) and Ultra-Wideband (UWB)—accurately classify respiratory behavior as normal or abnormal. This achieves a high accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 8. 1 7 \%}$</tex> on a test dataset comprising diverse respiratory patterns from various radar setups and target positions.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in $W$-Band GaAs MMIC Radar Sensors for High-Precision Vital Sign Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper introduces the recent advancements in W-band radar sensor technology, including self-injection-locked (SIL) and super-regenerative oscillator (SRO) systems. Utilizing GaAs monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) technology, both architectures demonstrate notable capabilities in vital sign monitoring applications, highlighted by their high sensitivity and low power consumption. SIL radars feature low hardware complexity and considerable sensitivity, whereas SRO systems provide enhanced sensitivity and reduced power usage. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of these W-band integrated radars, exhibiting the potential for accurate healthcare monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Wireless Electromagnetic Tracking System for Wireless Capsule Endoscope
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Electromagnetic tracking (EMT) is widely used in image-guided surgical procedures, enabling precise tracking of the position and orientation of medical instruments. However, the traditional wired EMT system needs wires to be led out from the transmitting side to the receiving side, rendering it unsuitable for tracking in vivo biomedical implants. This study proposes a 6-DoF wireless tracking hybrid method based on the EMT and inertial measurement unit.

articleTitle: Residue Amplifier Gain Error Duplication and Cancellation for Two-Step Pipelined ADCs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This article proposes Error Duplication and Cancellation (EDC) to tolerate the residue amplifier (RA) gain error in pipelined ADCs. EDC cancels the gain error of the RA by virtue of duplicating and subtracting the gain error in the analog domain, thus avoiding additional digital calibration circuitry and loops. EDC also obviates the need of a high-gain op amp and additional timing phases. Behavioral simulations of a 300-MHz, 12-bit two-step pipelined successive-approximationregister (SAR) ADC show EDC maintains a stable signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) over RA gain errors as large as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30$</tex>%, and improves the SNDR by nearly 7.2 dB with a 20% gain error. EDC improves the yield of the ADC from 47.3% to 98.9% over 1,000 runs of RA gain variations.

articleTitle: Asynchronous Optical Sampling Picosecond Ultrasonics of a GHz Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Biosensors are key technologies for diagnosis and drag development, where remote and real-time measurement is important. In this study, we developed an asynchronous optical sampling method to detect resonance frequency of nanofilms to detect proteins. Our method enables us to monitor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 30 \text{GHz}$</tex> and high-Q resonance. From the decrease in the resonance frequency, we detected 10 ng/ml rabbit immunoglobulin G.

articleTitle: Garment-Integrated Microwave Sensor for Sweat Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study presents a garment-integrated resonant microwave sensor for real-time sweat detection. By measuring the resonance frequency, the sensor detects varying moisture levels within fabrics, offering a reliable approach for garment moisture due to body sweating. The design separates the sensor tag from the reader, allowing a wireless sensing. When tested at room temperature, the sensor demonstrated a significant pole resonance frequency shift from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$378 \mathbf{M H z}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$258 \mathbf{M H z}$</tex> upon the absorption 0.5 mL of water in the fabric, with a direct predictable correlation with moisture content. This trend underscores the sensor's potential for precise, non-invasive sweat sensing within a wearable platform.

articleTitle: Diffusion Model-Based Assisted Attacks on Pufsecured Telematics and Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel approach leveraging Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) to enhance attacks on physically unclonable function (PUF) keys. PUFs generate secret binary keys that are electromagnetically unclonable and have demonstrated robustness against machine learning-based attacks, including Fourier regression and generative adversarial networks (GANs). Our method utilizes DDPMs to generate keys from pure noise or noisy signals, effectively replicating the secret keys extracted from integrated circuits. To optimize performance, we introduce modifications to the pre-processing and postprocessing stages. Specifically, the pre-processing step transitions the key representation from binary to grayscale before applying DDPM, while the post-processing stage incorporates a predefined threshold to binarize the generated keys. Experimental results demonstrate that our DDPM-based approach significantly outperforms GANs, achieving superior accuracy in key generation from noise. This work highlights the potential of DDPMs in assisted attacks by investigating noisy signals.

articleTitle: Physiological Radar-Based Sedentary State Classification using Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: While continuous-wave (CW) Doppler radar can be used to unobtrusively monitor human cardiopulmonary vital signs in uncontrolled settings, locomotion or other extraneous motion can sometimes obscure or distort such measurements. This work examines the application of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to classify sedentary and non-sedentary states, which would facilitate monitoring long-term variation of vital signs specifically limited to sedentary periods. Both Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) were applied to output signals from 2.4-GHz quadrature CW Doppler radar measurements of 12 subjects exhibiting sedentary and non-sedentary states. The findings indicate that applying RNNs directly to in-phase (I) and quadrature (Q) (not demodulated) radar outputs provided the most effective means of classifying subject state, acheiving accuracies greater than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 6 \%}$</tex>. These results clearly demonstrate the value of using RNNs for classifying physiological radar data for subjects that are free to move about, as well as their potential for analyzing quadrature radar without preliminary demodulation.

articleTitle: 24-GHz Single-Channel Continuous Wave Doppler Radar for Recognizing Diverse Breathing Patterns: A Feasibility Study
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Clinical monitoring of breathing patterns using non-invasive methods has gained significant attention due to its non-contact and unobtrusive nature. Previous research has explored various radar configurations, including quadrature channel continuous wave (CW) radar, frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar, and ultra-wideband (UWB) radar, to extract breathing patterns. However, a single-channel CW radar offers a simpler architecture and demands fewer signal processing chains compared to its quadrature radar counterpart. This paper evaluates the feasibility of using a 24-GHz single-channel CW radar to recognize three distinct human breathing patterns: normal, fast, and slow. Experimental results demonstrated that simpler-architecture single-channel CW radar could track these three different respiratory patterns with an average accuracy of 94.63% when compared to reference ground truth chest belts.

articleTitle: A 80 GHz GaN HEMT Amplifier Using Common Gate Topology Loading Open Stub at Gate
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: A 80 GHz amplifier was demonstrated using GaN HEMT which has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.15 \mu m$</tex> gate length and 100 GHz fmax. The amplifier applies gain boosting technique using open stub at the gate with common gate structure. Shorter length showed higher frequency response. The amplifier which had <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$310 \mu m$</tex> lengthstub showed 3.5dB at 82.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Beamforming System Assists in Human Body Moisture Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study explores a non-invasive approach to human body moisture content detection using millimeter wave (mm-Wave) technology. Millimeter waves have non-ionizing and non-contact characteristics, making them suitable for frequent physiological monitoring. It is particularly suitable for detecting water-related diseases such as congestive heart failure, lung fluid, and cancerous tissue. The signal reflection intensity of millimeter waves depends on the dielectric coefficient of the tissue, which can reflect different moisture contents. Beamforming technology is applied in the research to improve the signal strength in the target area and accurately measure the water content in the human body, providing a safe and reliable technical solution for clinical diagnosis and daily health monitoring.

articleTitle: Fall Detection Doppler Radar System Based on Time and Spatial Division
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This work demonstrates a 2.45-GHz beamswitching Doppler radar system for real-time human fall detection. By utilizing Butler matrixes for beam switching, the system divides the spatial coverage to distinguish different body regions. Combined with time-sequence information, it enables the continuous tracking of human motion, providing more comprehensive data for fall detection and analysis. Experimental results validate the feasibility and reliability of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Cylindrical Coplanar Waveguide Transition Circuit for Microwave Connections on Curved Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: External connections are critical in microwave circuits, and designing impedance-matched coaxial transitions is a key challenge. While planar circuit transitions are wellstudied, limited attention has been given to transitions for curved surfaces, such as vials and test tubes commonly encountered in chemical and biomedical laboratories. With the growing demand for accurate in-situ measurements in these applications, addressing this gap has become increasingly important. This work introduces a novel transition from coaxial to coplanar waveguide (CPW) mode on a cylindrical surface, specifically designed for use with curved containers like vials. The proposed transition achieves a minimum return loss of 12 dB within the DC- 10 GHz band and maintains an insertion loss below 1 dB up to 6 GHz. Fabricated on a semi-flexible substrate, the design is well-suited for biomedical sensing and in-situ measurements of cylindrical samples.

articleTitle: Integrated Single-Board 24 GHz FMCW Radar and Infrared Thermal Sensor Fusion for Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This work presents an integrated 24 GHz frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar and infrared thermal detection system designed for single-board sensor fusion. The system enables versatile target detection, including range tracking, thermal monitoring, and vibration frequency analysis. While the radar's operation in the mmWave regime provides enhanced spatial resolution and the ability to detect minute displacements, the higher frequency also makes it more susceptible to environmental interferences, such as moving objects and background vibrations. To address these challenges, an infrared module is incorporated for temperature measurements, effectively filtering out non-biological vibrations and isolating physiological signals. The system operates by transmitting radar signals to a device under test (DUT) and processing the reflected signals for range FFT analysis, determining the DUT's distance from the radar. Vibration frequencies are extracted from the radar signals, and phase demodulation is applied to establish a time-phase relationship for accurate monitoring. Experimental results demonstrate the radar-thermal sensor fusion system's capability to reliably monitor vibration frequencies across various distances and environmental conditions. By integrating thermal imaging, the system can be used to effectively distinguish physiological signals from living beings and periodic motions generated by non-living objects, making it a robust solution for diverse monitoring applications.

articleTitle: A Wearable Self-Powered Harmonic-Backscattering SWIPT Tag for Avalanche Rescue Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper introduces a wearable and selfpowered backscattering sensor tag with multifunctional operations of simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) for avalanche rescue operations. Specifically, the sensor tag is implemented on textile and constructed by a two-port dual-band antenna and a novel 90-degree hybrid coupler (HC) that features distinct signal flows at fundamental (f0) and second-harmonic (2f0) frequencies. By asymmetrically introducing two shorted quarter-wavelength stubs, half of the proposed HC branches feature band-stop responses at 2f0. Consequently, within a single compact structure, the proposed design could harvest the fundamental frequency (f0) to power the communication module via a full-wave rectifying circuit, while the victims’ health and location data is modulated and backscattered to the avalanche rescue transceiver carrying by the second harmonic frequency (2f0) generated from rectifying circuit due to its non-linear behavior. The numerical results show that the self-powering backscatter radio tag operates effectively at both fundamental and second harmonic frequencies. The power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the rectenna achieves nearly 70% and a second harmonic conversion loss (CL) of nearly 20.5 dB at an input RF power of 5 dBm. We envision that the proposed self-powered backscatter sensor tag may be beneficial for applications in personal localizing/sensing systems, and telemedicine healthcare.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: Unseen Imprint: Resonating Bio-Art Through RFID
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study presents an interactive bio-art utilizing RFID technology to explore critical issues such as genetic privacy, bio-information misuse, and societal biases. Drawing inspiration from the exhibit “Stranger Visions”, this work retains its core themes while transforming the artistic expression into an interactive format to enhance sensory engagement. Through integrating RF/microwave technology, this work demonstrates its potential not only to celebrate advance biomedical innovation but also to serve as a platform for addressing broader ethical and societal concerns.

articleTitle: Enhancing Muscle Performance and Recovery Assessment with MM-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study introduces a simulation-based method for evaluating muscle condition through mm-Wave RADAR technology, aiming to enable real-time analysis of muscle characteristics for assessing performance and recovery after physical activity. Leveraging the non-invasive and highresolution capabilities of mm-Wave RADAR, the research models and simulates the interaction between RADAR waves and muscle tissue using MATLAB. Key parameters such as signal reflection and muscle behavior are investigated to achieve precise muscle condition analysis without direct physical contact. The simulation results underscore the potential of mmWave RADAR in healthcare and sports science, offering an innovative approach to monitor the hydration, stress, and temperature levels of muscles during physical activity and optimizing recovery strategies. The findings highlight the promise of mm-Wave RADAR as a valuable tool for personalized health monitoring in both clinical and athletic settings.

articleTitle: Gait Parameters to Detect Parkinson's Disease Using a Radar Network: Preliminary Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: The early detection of Parkinson's disease (PD) is critical to increase the quality of life of the patients. Radar technology is a strong candidate to anticipate its detection by monitoring gait. However, no study has pointed out which gait parameters are the most relevant to detect PD using radars. In this paper, the gait of two healthy individuals and three patients with PD is compared using a radar network to determine which gait parameters are more determinant to detect PD. This effect is quantified for three different gait paces. The results show that the mean and maximum stride times when the subjects walk at their regular pace are the most determinant to detect PD. This contribution is relevant for radar network implementations to detect PD, as it addresses which parameters should be analyzed during clinical assessments.

articleTitle: Hybrid Signal Processing Framework Based on Second-Order Differentiation and Harmonic Superposition for Non-Contact Heart Rhythm Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: In this article, a novel method was proposed to extract heartbeat information based on a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order differential technique complemented by leveraging the elevated strong harmonics of heartbeat in frequency domain signal by superimposing their magnitude to the fundamental frequency. A theoretical analysis of the working principle of the algorithm has been provided, along with a simulation, to demonstrate the algorithm's advantage in the existence of strong respiration harmonics. An experimental analysis was conducted, and the accuracy achieved using the proposed method was 1.47 Bpm for five subjects with a mean average error of over two minutes of collected data.

articleTitle: Frequency Tunable Filtering Power Divider With Arbitrary Power Division Ratio and Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of filtering power divider (FPD) with tunable center frequency and an arbitrary power division ratio. The proposed FPD is designed using two dual-mode resonators and exhibits high frequency selective characteristics by generating transmission zeros on either side of passbands. The passband frequency can be continuously tuned by adjusting even and odd-mode resonant frequencies of dual-mode resonators. To validate the design, a microstrip line FPD with equal power divider ratio is designed and fabricated. The experimental results show that the passband frequency is tuned from 1.35 GHz to 1.90 GHz by adjusting single dc-bias voltage of varactor diode. The in-band transmission insertion loss is remained between 1.30 dB and 2.34 dB (excluding inherent loss of power divider) while maintaining frequency selective characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of Quarter-Mode SIW BPF with Ultra-Wide Stopband and Impedance Matching Functionality
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the design of quartermode (QM) substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) bandpass filter (BPF) with ultra-wide stopband and impedance matching functionality. Ultra-wide stopband characteristics can be obtained by embedding dumbbell shape slots (DSS) on the ground metal plane at the input and output ends of the proposed BPF to suppress spurious response of higher modes. The matching functionality can be achieved by detuning the resonance frequencies of the first or last QM SIW resonators due to the reactive components of the complex termination impedances. For concept validation, a two-stage QM SIW BPF is designed and fabricated with the center frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(f_{0}\right)$</tex> of 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{G H z}$</tex> and the termination impedances of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(20+j 15) \Omega$</tex>-to-50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex>. The minimum attenuation level of 26.7 dB is measured from DC to 7.2 GHz at the lower stopband and 12.85 GHz to 40 GHz at the higher stopband. Since the proposed SIW BPF is realized using QM SIW cavity, the circuit size is much smaller compared to the SIW BPF realized using full-mode SIW cavity.

articleTitle: Experiment Setup Design for In-Vivo Microwave Spectroscopy of Galleria Mellonella Larvae
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This work introduces the use of microwave dielectric spectroscopy for in-vivo quantitative and objective characterization of Galleria Mellonella larvae to assess their potential as animal models in biotoxicity and pathogenesis studies. Coaxial probe measurements are performed between 1 GHz and 26.5 GHz for control larvae and ethanol-injected larvae. An experimental setup is developed to enhance measurement repeatability. While the setup improves measurement consistency, it cannot yet detect significant differences between control larvae and ethanolinjected larvae.

articleTitle: A New Radio-Frequency Microfluidic Injection-Locked Oscillator Sensor for Loss Tangent Measurement of Liquid Material
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: A new radio-frequency microfluidic injectionlocked oscillator (ILO) sensor is proposed in this paper for loss tangent measurement of the liquid material. The proposed sensor comprises a passive T-shape LC resonator (TLCR) sensing structure and an ILO. When an RF signal passes through the TLCR loaded by a test liquid, its amplitude will be decreased by the liquid's loss. The degraded signal is injected into an ILO to vary the output power. By loading different test liquids into the microfluidic channel, one can measure the ILO's output powers to relate the corresponding liquids' loss tangents. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.5-\mu \mathbf{L}$</tex> water-ethanol mixtures with ethanol volume fractions of 20 % to 80 % in increments of 20 % are used as the test liquids to evaluate the sensor performance. Compared with the results obtained from a dielectric probe, the maximum error of the loss tangent measured by the proposed sensor is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-3.8 \%$</tex>.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of WSN System for Wireless EEG Using Sub-cm Sized 2-GHz Domino-Resonator
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: As a future wireless electroencephalography (EEG) system with dense sensor nodes (SNs), we propose a wireless sensor network (WSN) system with sub-cm sized 2GHz domino-resonator. The 2 GHz RF carrier signal is transmitted from the signal source to the receiver through the domino-resonator with sub-cm sized coils. Each coil is equipped with a sensor and an amplitude shift keying (ASK) modulator. Since the RF carrier signal is ASK modulated by the sensor's data as each resonator, the data of each SN can be received by the receiver of domino-resonator system. By assigning different clock (CLK) frequencies to each SN, the ASK modulated signals can be identified and demodulated separately even if the number of SNs increases. The carrier signal transmission using sub-cm sized domino-resonator is discussed with the measurements of fabricated dominoresonator without modulator and the simulation of expected degradation by the RF switch losses. The design method of CLK frequencies is also described and verified by the simulation. These results show the feasibility of proposed wireless EEG system having (1) 7 cm total communication range (RF source to receiver distance) with every 7 mm SNs placement, and (2) 150 kbps data rate for each SN. This SN configuration has no RF oscillator for each SN and no wire connection between SNs will bring low power consumption and wearability which is suited for future dense EEG monitoring system.

articleTitle: Advanced Transmitter Coil Optimization Framework for Maximizing Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency in Small Animal Experimental Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: In small animal experimental platforms, wireless power transfer (WPT) is challenged with low efficiency and unsteadiness due to the free-positioning of animals. In this work, a novel transmitter (Tx) coil optimization procedure is proposed, which can achieve maximum transmission efficiency at required uniformity levels. By decomposition of the Tx coil into basis current density modes, the optimal Tx coil design can be found without a pre-defined geometry. Three optimized coils (Coils X/Y/Z) produce uniform magnetic field (B-field) along three orthogonal axes respectively. Through linear superposition of the Tx coils, three-dimensional (3-D) omni-directional WPT for freely moving animal experiments can be achieved. The prototype system is measured to provide 5 % to 10 % transmission efficiency to a single Rx coil at the measurement points.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Switch Mode Amplifiers for Low-Field MRI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper examines a switch mode amplifier and compares it to a linear amplifier in a low-field MRI system. Results show that digital amplifiers provide comparable receive signal qualities and are suitable for MRI applications, with minimal differences in SNR, but emphasize the general applicability in low-field MRI applications.

articleTitle: A Long Range Small Tag Antenna on Human Healthcare with 3D Printed Artificial Substrate
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study presents an innovative, low-cost miniaturized tag antenna with an artificial substrate, optimized for use on the human body. Perfect impedance matching between the proposed antenna and the microchip was obtained by adjusting the gap's capacitive reactance. A design approach based on current distribution along the dipole antenna arms was applied to further reduce the antenna's size. As a result, the proposed antenna configuration not only achieved miniaturization but also enhanced radiation efficiency to 33.2 %, attained a gain of -1.68 dB, and reached a power transmission coefficient of approximately 99.4 %. Additionally, it provided an extended reading distance (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>\mathbf{1 2} \mathbf{\ m}$</tex>) and a wide impedance bandwidth of 30 MHz, spanning nearly the entire UHF RFID frequency range used in North America, regardless of the tag's placement on the human body.

articleTitle: A Switched Fast-Startup Ac-Coupled Amplifier for Low-Distortion Detection of Human Vital Signs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Microwave radar sensors have been used as wireless vital sign sensors for some time. After down-conversion to baseband, the radar output signals often require amplification before being digitized. AC-coupled amplifiers offer a simpler overall architecture compared to dc-coupled systems but suffer from long start times when used with frequencies in the range of human vital signs. Previous fast-start circuits have improved start time but introduce distortion at low frequencies. This paper proposes a new ac-coupled baseband amplifier architecture that uses switched MOSFETs to provide faster start time without impacting low frequency performance. The system theory shows its ability to improve start time, while experimental results using a benchtop and radar system demonstrate that the amplifier offers a simple and low-cost method of reducing start time without introducing distortion.

articleTitle: Underwater Communication Using Thin Flexible Microdome-Structured PVDF Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: We present a lightweight, flexible PVDF film transducer with microdome structures designed for underwater communication. The transducer was evaluated through frequency response analysis, acoustic signal testing, and transmission of a digital image. The transducer exhibited a consistent output across a wide frequency range, with peaks indicating efficient signal transmission. Spectrogram analysis confirmed its ability to transmit complex signals with high fidelity, supported by SSIM evaluation showing a maximum value of 0.59108 at 4 VPP. These results highlight the transducer's potential for energy-efficient, high-fidelity underwater communication.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Millimeter-Wave Power Divider Circuit for Capsule Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper designs a 1 × 2 power divider for millimeter waves and applies it to the capsule. The power divider uses a T-junction structure to achieve the high bandwidth advantage of 34.6-40.9 GHz. Simulation results confirm that the power divider circuit design can operate in different environments and is not susceptible to the effects of the capsule and human tissues. The proposed power divider can be quickly integrated with various antennas and applied in capsules through a simple size structure.

articleTitle: High-Gain Slot Array Antenna Integrated on Aluminum Nitride Ceramic Substrate for SubTerahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This article proposes a 1 × 2 slot array antenna suitable for sub-terahertz (sub-THz). The antenna integrates the slot array antenna and the WR6.5-SIW transition structure on the Aluminum nitride (AlN) substrate with the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) structure. The good dielectric properties of the AIN substrate enable the antenna to cover 133.2-134.3 GHz and reach a peak gain of 13.3 dBi. At the same time, integrating antennas on a single-layer plane substrate can reduce the production costs and improve the practicality of the sub-THz.

articleTitle: A Three-Channel Reflected SH-SAW Biosensor for Cardiovascular Risk Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a global health challenge, with biomarkers such as apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) and apolipoprotein B (ApoB) playing a critical role in risk assessment. This study introduces a novel three-channel shear horizontal surface acoustic wave (SH-SAW) biosensor for point-of-care testing (POCT) of CVD biomarkers. Utilizing a reflected-type sensor design, the system achieves high sensitivity and low noise by optimizing the reflector arrangement, reducing signal loss and production costs. The biosensor simultaneously detects ApoA1 and ApoB using independent sensing channels, with one channel as a reference. Its compact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 \text{mm} \times 5 \text{mm}$</tex> chip integrates epoxy and glass protection to ensure durability and liquid resistance. The platform employs real-time slope signal analysis for rapid detection of lipid profiles, eliminating the need for secondary enhancement even at high analyte concentrations. Comparative studies reveal strong correlations with clinical results <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R=0.965$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A p o B$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R=0.890$</tex> for ApoA1) and detection limits of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.01 \text{mg} / \text{dL}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.597 \text{mg} / \text{dL}$</tex>, respectively. These advancements position the SH-SAW biosensor as a rapid, cost-effective, and portable solution for personalized health management and preventive medicine.

articleTitle: Microwave Resonant Imaging for Subcutaneous Tissue Detection Using Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This work introduces a refined image-processing method explicitly designed to amalgamate raster-scanned images obtained with a compact planar microwave resonator. The resonator tuned for use on the skin provides a deeper field penetration into the dermis layer, compared to the skin impedance measurements. The resonance of the sensor is sensitive to the dielectric properties of the tissues underneath the skin. Healthy and abnormal tissues exhibit different dielectric characteristics. Pixelated images can leverage resonant frequencies and reflection coefficients to enhance contrasts and boundaries to identify the abnormal tissues. We proposed using analytical tools like the structural similarity index to correlate frequency shifts with reflection coefficient magnitudes precisely. Preliminary results suggested the adeptness of the technique at classifying whether the tissue depth surpasses 15 mm and detecting tumor locations with a high accuracy when the image depth does not exceed 15 mm. A compact neural network model was implemented for processing the microwave images when the tumor depth exceeded 15 mm and achieved a high Dice coefficient. The work incorporated simulations to substantiate the novel concept and demonstrated its potential for noninvasive, efficient, and cost-effective subcutaneous imaging in medical applications.

articleTitle: Time-Constant Induced Memory Effect for Biomedical Radar Vital Signs Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Applications of Doppler radar for vital signs have been studied and investigated for a long time, and significant strides towards implementing Doppler radar sensors for such applications have been made in recent years. Designing optimum hardware component values for AC coupling and baseband signal amplification for radar sensing applications remains challenging. The selection of capacitor value for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A C$</tex> coupling has a significant impact on the accuracy of small movement detection due to the memory effect induced by the time constant. In this paper, a study on the induced timeconstant memory issue on data due to intermittent shifts in signal from radar has been conducted, and analysis regarding the correct selection of capacitor values to mitigate the problem is proposed via simulation and verified by experimental analysis.

articleTitle: Radar2Text: Generation of Linguistic Summary from mmWave Radar Signatures Using Fine-Tuned Multimodal Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) sensing technology enables the perception and measurement of the physical world in a non-invasive and privacy-preserving manner. However, radar signals are inherently non-intuitive, requiring specialized expertise to process datasets and interpret system observations. To address these challenges, this paper explores the feasibility of leveraging fine-tuned Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to extract critical and accurate textual descriptions from radar-generated range history images. By fine-tuning a multimodal foundation model, the study establishes a connection between radar signatures captured when a target moves away and toward a radar and their corresponding textual descriptions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, highlighting the potential of mmWave radar technology for natural language-based multimodal target tracking.

articleTitle: A K-Band VCO using a Transformer-Based Resonance Tank for Biomedical Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave widetuning range voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) fabricated using the TSMC 90-nm CMOS process. A low phase noise (PN) and wide-tuning range performance can be achieved by utilizing a noise filter inductor and a transformer-based resonator. The transformer-based resonator increases the tuning range by doubling the bias range of the varactor and boosts the quality factor of the resonator tank through impedance transformation. A 2-bit capacitor bank is also used to achieve reasonable VCO gain (Kvco). The proposed VCO achieves a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2 7. 5 \%}$</tex> tuning range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$19.5-25.8 \text{GHz}$</tex> while consuming 7.9 to 8.6 mW. It realizes a phase noise of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{- 1 0 2. 6} \mathbf{\ d B c} / \mathbf{H z}$</tex> at a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \mathbf{\ M H z}$</tex> offset and a figure of merit with a tuning range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\text{FOM}_{\mathrm{T}}\right)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{- 1 8 9. 5 \text{ dBc } / \text{ Hz } \text {. }. \text {. } \text{ d }}$</tex>

articleTitle: Improving Frequency Sweep Linearity in FMCW Vital Sign Radar Using Frequency Locking
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Conventional voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) based frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) vital sign radars often suffer from nonlinear frequency sweeps. The nonlinearity distorts the beat frequency of the radar's baseband output signal and lead to inaccurate distance measurements. To address this issue, this work developed a novel FMCW vital sign radar that incorporates a frequency-locked loop (FLL). The frequency locking mechanism of the FLL effectively mitigates the frequency sweep nonlinearity of a VCO, thereby improving the accuracy of distance detection. Experimental results demonstrated that incorporating FLL into an FMCW vital sign radar effectively reduced the distance detection error by up to 9.5% for a 2-meter range.

articleTitle: Optimized IRS Positioning for Phase-Tuned Wireless Physiological Motion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper explores the impact of physical positioning of Intelligent Reflective Surfaces (IRS) on enhancing physiological motion detection in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Operating at 28 GHz with an Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) scheme, the proposed system incorporates a static IRS whose physical placement is systematically adjusted to optimize signal propagation and phase alignment. Experimental results reveal that precise IRS positioning significantly improves detection accuracy, with peak-to-peak (P2P) phase shifts increasing by 57 % in the perpendicular configuration and 56 % in the parallel configuration, corresponding to optimal signal reflections. These findings demonstrate the potential of physically repositioning IRS to achieve superior sensitivity and robustness in wireless physiological sensing, paving the way for advanced positioning algorithms and applications in complex multipath environments.

articleTitle: A Comparison between WIPD and PCB Flip-Chip Packaging for Broadband MFCW Agile Radar in Vital-Sign Detection Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Previous work, MFCW Radar for vital sign detection, has been done in our lab. The receiver front-end and the signal source are manufactured using a 180-nm CMOS process, packaged on RO4003C printed-circuit board(PCB) through wire bonding. However, the package carrier and the bonding wire degrade the performance of the radar above 20 GHz. To improve the radar performance, the package method, flip-chip, was implemented to reduce pass losses. At the same time, we compare two different package carriers, the traditional RO4003C printed-circuit board (PCB) and the WIN Integrated Passive Device (WIPD). The WIPD demonstrates superior design flexibility. The measurements showed that using WIPD with flip-chip packaging by the gold bump achieved conversion gains comparable to direct on-wafer measurement.

articleTitle: Multirate Filtering for Pulsatile Bioimpedance Signals with MHz Excitation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Pulsatile bioimpedance measurements require filters with very narrow bandwidths to preserve heartbeat-rate modulation while suppressing excess noise. At the signal's carrier frequency, this demands an impractically-high-Q filter. Multirate signal processing is an attractive solution to this problem, as it provides an avenue to extract the signals of interest practically. This paper presents a multirate filtering solution and shows step-by-step how the bioimpedance data of interest are extracted from noise and excitation frequency in in-phase and quadrature signals acquired from an analog measurement circuit. The tested impedance values resemble realistic human tissue impedance, demonstrating the method's ability to measure a human pulse within an approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50-\text{Hz}$</tex> bandwidth at a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-\text{MHz}$</tex> carrier. This method is useful for high-Q bioimpedance measurements where interest lies in the details of signals pulsing at the rate of a beating human heart.

articleTitle: Autonomous Integrated Sensing and Processing for Bioradar: Advancing Non-Invasive Biomedical Monitoring and Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel automated system that leverages a Raspberry Pi to operate a 24 GHz single-channel continuous wave (CW) radar for through-the-wall concurrent vital sign monitoring of two subjects. The system autonomously performs independent component analysis using the joint approximation diagonalization of eigenmatrices (ICA-JADE) to separate both individuals' breathing rates (BR). It applies the maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform (MODWT) after ICA-JADE to extract heart rates (HR). By integrating the radar system and ICA-JADE into an embedded platform, the system operates without requiring manual intervention. The automation framework enables real-time processing, enhancing the system's practical deployment in real-world applications. The results demonstrate high accuracy in isolating BR and HR using ICA-JADE, as benchmarked against conventional chest belts and ECG measurements. This fully automated approach shows significant potential for applications such as search and rescue operations, security surveillance, and remote healthcare monitoring through barriers.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystal RIS Integrated with SIL Radar for NLOS Vital Sign Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel liquid crystal (LC) reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) integrated with a self-injection-locked (SIL) radar system for vital sign monitoring in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) regions. The LC RIS dynamically reconfigures wavefronts using phase modulation to enable precise target localization, while the SIL radar enhances sensitivity and reduces system complexity. The LC RIS design incorporates printed dipole antennas and differential lines to facilitate effective beamforming. Experimental results validate the system's accuracy and efficiency in NLOS vital sign monitoring.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection for Identity Authentication Using 1D-CNN-LSTM Autoencoder and Doppler Radar with Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study presents an integrated framework combining 1D-CNN-LSTM-Autoencoder-based anomaly detection with identity authentication using machine learning classifiers. The 1D-CNN-LSTM Autoencoder enhances system reliability by identifying and excluding faulty intervals in timeseries data caused by system instability or random movements. The dataset, collected under a controlled protocol, features scenarios such as Resting and Valsalva maneuvers for training and testing. To address measurement data interference, which can affect identity recognition accuracy, anomaly detection filters out corrupted signals, maintaining system stability and reliability. Among the machine learning classifiers, Cubic SVM demonstrated superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 8 8. 7 %. This integrated approach enhances system robustness, offering promising applications in secure access control, smart environments, and healthcare monitoring.

articleTitle: Toward Clinically Accurate Continuous Blood Pressure Smart Watch Biosensors Using Equitable Bioimpedance Modality and AI
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Current wearable blood pressure monitors using photoplethysmography (PPG) in wrist watches or rings face accuracy issues with darker skin tones, leading to biased AI algorithms and inequitable health monitoring. We propose a smartwatch-integrable, lowpower wearable antenna biosensor measuring bioimpedance (BioZ) changes from radial artery blood flow using radio frequencies (RF) for continuous blood pressure estimation. This non-contact RF BioZ-based approach offers a more equitable solution across diverse demographics. Our device has shown good performance with mean absolute errors (MAE) of 5.67 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 6.05 \text{mmHg}$</tex> for RF BioZ. It meets British Hypertension Society (BHS) and Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI) error threshold requirements for grade <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A /$</tex> passing score for non-cuff-based BP measuring technology, respectively.

articleTitle: A 200-GHz Signal Source in 40-nm CMOS for Sub-THz Biomedical Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This work proposes a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200-\text{GHz}$</tex> signal source for sub-THz biomedical imaging applications. The signal source integrates a fundamental voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), a power amplifier (PA), and a frequency doubler. Its architecture is optimized for a wide tuning range and high output power. The PA amplifies the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100-\text{GHz}$</tex> signal generated by the VCO, providing sufficient power to drive the frequency doubler, which then multiplies the input frequency to produce the desired <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2 0 0 - G H z}$</tex> output. Implemented in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40-\text{nm}$</tex> CMOS technology, the proposed signal source delivers an output power of -0.3 dBm at 181.4 GHz with a tuning range of 8.5 %. The signal source only consumes 172 mW from a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.9-\mathrm{V}$</tex> supply.

articleTitle: Four-Channel Pqsil Radar for Remote Vital Sign Monitoring with Clutter Effect
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This study proposes a 2.4 GHz four-channel phase- and quadrature self-injection-locked radar for vital sign monitoring in cluttered environments. Effective clutter immunity was achieved using modified principal component analysis (MPCA) and channel compression demodulation (CCD). MPCA mitigates clutter by reorganizing signals and canceling out unwanted components, while CCD compresses trajectories, making it less sensitive to clutter. Displacement monitoring experiments of human chest motion at a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3-\mathrm{m}$</tex> range demonstrated that both methods successfully extracted respiration and heart rates, even in cluttered environments.

articleTitle: Investigation of Breast Tumor Size Effects for Microwave Breast Imaging with Ultra-Wideband Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common invasive cancer in women and a leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Tumor size plays a crucial role in diagnosis and staging. This study investigates the impact of tumor size on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S 2 1}$</tex> transmission signal and specific absorption rate (SAR) distribution in a 3D breast model simulated in COMSOL Multiphysics using an ultra-wideband (UWB) microstrip antenna. The results show that energy concentration increases with tumor size, with larger tumors showing broader SAR distributions. At a frequency of 3.1 GHz, an inverse relationship between SAR and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S 21$</tex> is observed; smaller tumors exhibit lower SAR values and stronger S21 signals, while larger tumors demonstrate higher SAR values and reduced S21 signals.

articleTitle: Clinical Imaging by the Microwave Mammography
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: We have developed a microwave imaging system that solves the inverse scattering problem by implementing an imaging sensor consisting of a highly sensitive dielectric-loaded dual-polarized horn antenna and an equipment calibration method using two phantoms. Clinical imaging of breast cancer patients was performed. Early cancer in high-density breast tissue, which is difficult to diagnose with X-ray mammography, was able to be detected.

articleTitle: Multi-Harmonic Amplitude Analysis of Space-Time-Coding Direct Antenna Modulation for Target Angle Estimation and Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a new kind of space-time-coding (STC)-enabled direction-finding approach for human target localization in smart healthcare environments. The method overcomes the limitations of angular detection coverage constrained by monotonic linear regions by utilizing multi-harmonic amplitude analysis of STC harmonics. Angular information is estimated by selecting and averaging the nearest angle data points across harmonic power-level differences and angle mapping sets, leveraging the STC harmonic beam steering features. Experimental validation on a direct antenna modulation (DAM)-enabled STC array confirms the effectiveness of the proposed angle estimation method and demonstrates its ability to extract vital signs from the respective STC harmonics.

articleTitle: Quasi-Elliptic Tunable Bandpass Filter With Controllable Transmission Zero Locations
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a design of quasi-elliptic bandpass filter (BPF) with center frequency tunability characteristics. To achieve quasi-elliptic response, transmission zeros (TZs) are generated at the lower and upper sides of the passband through cross-coupling between the first resonator and output port, while the location of these TZs are controllable. Frequency tunability can be achieved by tuning the resonance frequency of tunable resonators. To validate the design, a prototype of the microstrip line of the proposed structure is designed, manufactured, and measured. The measurement results show that passband center frequency is tuned from 1.65 GHz to 1.95 GHz, achieving tuning ratios of 1.182:1. In all tuning states, in-band minimum insertion loss is varying from 2.64 to 3.18 dB, while return loss is better than 11.67 dB.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Detection Based on Modified-RLMD Algorithm in the Presence of Random Body Movement Using FMCW Radars
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: The Modified-Robust Local Mean Decomposition (mRLMD) method is introduced as a novel approach for heart rate extraction using a Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar system. Based on RLMD, mRLMD utilizes the local median, instead of local mean to minimize the impact of outliers, significantly improving accuracy in challenging conditions. The proposed algorithm is designed to accurately extract heart rate under large-scale random body movement (RBM). By combining an Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), a matched filter and differential enhancement, the proposed mRLMD algorithm effectively suppresses RBM and other low-frequency components, such as respiration harmonics, while amplifying the heartbeat signal. Measurement results show that the method achieves an average relative heart rate error of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${1.98 \%}$</tex>, demonstrating its reliability.

articleTitle: Heartbeat Detection Using Static RIS-Assisted mmWave OFDM System: A Channel State Information Approach with Software-Defined Radios
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel vital-sign monitoring system for heartbeat detection by incorporating a static reconfigurable intelligent surface within a millimeter-wave (mmWave) OFDM communication framework. The system begins by generating an OFDM waveform, which is transmitted using the software-defined radio in combination with the mmWave frequency up/down-converters and the beamforming modules. The transceiver is designed as a double-conversion architecture. The OFDM signal with carrier frequency of 4.7 GHz is upconverted to 28 GHz and directed to the RIS through beamforming. The RIS, characterized by a gain of 29.1 dBi with a feeding antenna at 0.6 m, reflects the signal toward a stationary subject. A 10-second measurement interval is analyzed by estimating the channel state information, followed by Fourier transformation to extract the heartbeat frequency. Validation is performed by comparing the measured heartbeat rate with results from an Apple Watch, achieving a mean error of 3.6 bpm (4.06%). Furthermore, the communication performance of the system is evaluated, demonstrating an error vector magnitude (EVM) below 1.5 % and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 37 dB. The proposed system showcases the potential of RIS-assisted mmWave communication for integrated communication and health monitoring.

articleTitle: A Study of Continuous Noninvasive RF Hydration Sensing on Human Forearm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: In this work, a planar radio-frequency sensor is developed for noninvasive and efficient monitoring of water content variations in human body and tissues. The sensor operates on the principle of electromagnetic resonance, which is highly sensitive to changes in dielectric properties influenced by water content. Designed on a FR4 substrate, the planar loop resonator, tuned with an embedded metal pad, features enhanced resonance performance, compactness, sensitivity and wearability. Experiments conducted to monitor hydration processes on the forearm of a human subject at different days demonstrate the sensor ability to detect distinct trends as an individual's transition from dehydrated to hydrated states. The sensor's small, planar form factor offers promising potential for integration into a wearable device to be worn on the human forearm, enabling continuous and reliable hydration monitoring.

articleTitle: Respiratory Pattern Variability Assessment Using Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Biomedical Conference (IMBioC)
abstract: Respiratory process has a complex variability that can reflect the fundamental mechanisms of generating respiratory patterns, influence of emotion, association of cortical neuronal networks and may hold important physiologic and/or diagnostic information. This paper focuses on studying the capability of Doppler radar in assessing the respiration pattern variability (RPV) with a comprehensive reference of marker based Infrared camera system. The results show that RPV assessment using radar is in good agreement with those measured at various points of the torso using the infrared camera system.
